Name: e1_open_000
Text: Radio static. A phone voicemail, timestamped Sunday, 23:52.

Name: e1_open_001
Speaker: NILA
Text: Anna, naan dhaan. Station-ku call pannadha, okay? Plan panna maadhiri Tuesday vandhudu.
Subtitle: Anna, it's me. Don't call the station, okay? Just come Tuesday like we planned.

Name: e1_open_002
Speaker: NILA
Text: Naan oru vishayam kandupidichiruken. Phone-la solla mudiyaadhu. Inga vandhappo edhavadhu weird-aa irundha, Ruth kitta mattum pesu.
Subtitle: I found something. I can't say it on the phone. If anything feels weird when you get here, talk only to Ruth.

Name: e1_open_003
Speaker: NILA
Text: Anna, yaara venaalum nambu, aana andha—
Subtitle: Anna, trust anyone, but don't trust the—

Name: e1_open_004
Text: The message cuts. Silence.

Name: e1_apt_000
Text: A small one-bedroom near the river. A whiteboard of job applications, half of them crossed out. A graduation photo from the University of Windsor. On the counter: a box of laddu and mysore pak, a packet of clay diyas, and a gift-wrapped ham radio with a crooked bow.

Name: e1_apt_001
Text: You play the voicemail again. You call Nila. Straight to voicemail. Again.

Name: e1_apt_002
Text: Before you leave, you look around the flat one more time.

Name: e1_thought_pack1_000
Speaker: MANI
Text: Nila enna solla vandhaa? Oru vela edhavadhu prachanaiya?
Subtitle: What was Nila trying to tell me? Is something wrong?

Name: e1_call_000
Text: Your laptop rings. A video call from Vellore. Amma and Appa, 7 pm their time, Appa still in his shop shirt from Sri Valli Leathers.

Name: e1_call_001
Speaker: AMMA
Text: Kanna, saaptiya? Moonji ellam ilachu pochu.
Subtitle: Kanna, did you eat? Your face has gone so thin.

Name: e1_call_002
Speaker: MANI
Text: Saapten, Amma.
Subtitle: I ate, Amma.

Name: e1_call_003
Speaker: APPA
Text: Company-la irundhu edhavadhu news? Andha Thursday interview?
Subtitle: Any news from the company? That Thursday interview?

Name: e1_call_004
Speaker: MANI
Text: Second round, Appa. Thursday dhaan.
Subtitle: Second round, Appa. On Thursday.

Name: e1_call_005
Speaker: AMMA
Text: Nila enga? Moonu naala phone edukkala. En mela kovama irukkaala?
Subtitle: And Nila? Three days she hasn't picked up. Is she angry with me?

Name: e1_call2_000
Speaker: APPA
Text: Sweets eduthutu po. Kadai nalla poguthu, kavala padaadhenu Appa sonnaarnu sollu. Pongal-ku veetuku vara sollu.
Subtitle: Take her the sweets. Tell her Appa says the shop is doing fine, she should stop worrying. Tell her to come home for Pongal.

Name: e1_call2_001
Speaker: AMMA
Text: Innoru vishayam, Kanna. Preethi-nu oru ponnu, Windsor-la dhaan irukkaa. Pharmacist. Photo anupparen, paaru.
Subtitle: One more thing, Kanna. There's a girl called Preethi, she lives in Windsor too. A pharmacist. I'm sending her photo, have a look.

Name: e1_call2_002
Speaker: MANI
Text: Amma! Ippo venaam!
Subtitle: Amma! Not now!

Name: e1_call2_003
Text: Amma laughs. Appa shakes his head. The call ends. Your phone buzzes: a photo from Amma. You don't open it. You pick up the gift radio and look at it for a long moment.

Name: e1_road_000
Text: You head east along Lake Erie. Greenhouses glitter outside Leamington. Flat farmland, grain silos, a hawk on a fence post. The radio plays a country station you'd never admit to liking.

Name: e1_road_001
Text: At a red light you text Nila's flatmate, a name she's mentioned a hundred times.

Name: e1_road_002
Speaker: MANI
Text: Hi Tess, it's Mani, Nila's brother. Is she around? Coming up today.

Name: e1_road_003
Text: No reply. The light goes green. Your stomach says coffee.

Name: e1_tp1_000
Text: A busy coffee-and-donut shop. Red-and-cream decor, a hockey rerun on the TV, the smell of burnt sugar. You order a coffee and an apple fritter.

Name: e1_tp1_001
Text: At the counter, an old man in a flat cap slaps a receipt down.

Name: e1_tp1_002
Speaker: HAROLD
Text: Third day running! I order a double-double and somebody gives me decaf! I've been coming here since 1974!

Name: e1_tp1_003
Text: The young cashier, Priya, looks helpless. Your coffee is still brewing. You have nothing better to do.

Name: e1_tp1skip_000
Text: You try. You really do. But Harold is now shouting at the menu board, and Priya looks like she might cry, and you are a person who cannot leave a broken thing alone.

Name: e1_tp1skip_001
Speaker: MANI
Text: Can I see the receipts?

Name: e1_tp1p_000
Text: Small mystery: The Decaf Problem.

Name: e1_tp1acc_000
Text: So who's switching Harold's coffee?

Name: e1_tp1done_000
Speaker: JUNE
Text: The doctor said no caffeine after his heart thing, and he's a stubborn old goat!

Name: e1_tp1done_001
Speaker: HAROLD
Text: June! Fifty-two years and you're sabotaging my coffee?

Name: e1_tp1done_002
Speaker: JUNE
Text: Fifty-two years and I'd like fifty-three, thank you.

Name: e1_tp1done_003
Text: They bicker. Then they laugh. Then Harold, grumbling, drinks the decaf. Priya slides your fritter across the counter for free.

Name: e1_tp1done_004
Speaker: PRIYA
Text: You should be a detective.

Name: e1_tp1done_005
Speaker: MANI
Text: I'm a data guy. It's just logs.

Name: e1_shoulder_000
Text: Farmland turns to forest. The sky goes the colour of wet concrete. Your phone buzzes. Tess.

Name: e1_shoulder_001
Speaker: TESS
Text: haven't seen her since sunday night. thought she was with u?? her phone is here at the flat

Name: e1_shoulder_002
Text: You pull onto the gravel shoulder. You call Nila. Voicemail. You call again. Voicemail.

Name: e1_shoulder_003
Text: A truck blows past and rocks the car. You realise you're gripping the wheel hard enough to hurt.

Name: e1_shoulder_004
Speaker: MANI
Text: Okay. Okay. Drive.

Name: e1_tp2_000
Text: A quieter Tom Portons beside a gas station. Rain on the windows. A refrigerated box truck outside: MERROW PALLETS & SUPPLY.

Name: e1_tp2_001
Text: Inside, a burly man in a diner apron under his jacket is arguing with a teenage employee.

Name: e1_tp2_002
Speaker: GUS
Text: I left the cooler on the seat for two minutes. Two minutes!

Name: e1_tp2_003
Text: At the window table, a well-dressed man in a tailored wool coat and a silver watch sips black coffee and watches with mild amusement.

Name: e1_tp2b_000
Text: As you reach the staff room, the man in the wool coat is suddenly beside you, as if this were a game you were playing together.

Name: e1_tp2b_001
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Kids think every cooler is full of beer. Shall we?

Name: e1_tp2b_002
Text: The cooler is in the wet backpack. He gets to it first and lifts the lid an inch. You glimpse a heat pack and a ventilated plastic box with something coiled inside. He shuts it.

Name: e1_tp2b_003
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Bait. Gus fishes. Don't you, Gus?

Name: e1_tp2b_004
Speaker: GUS
Text: Yeah. Bait.

Name: e1_tp2b_005
Text: Gus takes the cooler without meeting your eyes and leaves fast. The truck pulls out into the rain.

Name: e1_victor_000
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Sharp eyes. What do you do?

Name: e1_victor_001
Speaker: MANI
Text: Software. Data. Between jobs.

Name: e1_victor_002
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Ah. The most dangerous kind of person. Someone who notices patterns. Where are you headed?

Name: e1_victor2_000
Text: His eyes go to your car through the window. The sweets box on the passenger seat.

Name: e1_victor2_001
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Diwali. Festival of lights. Good triumphs over evil, isn't it? I've always liked that story.

Name: e1_victor2_002
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: If north means the lake country, try Greyhaven. Fog, a lake, a priest who rings a bell for nobody. Lovely.

Name: e1_victor2_003
Text: His phone buzzes. He turns half away.

Name: e1_victor2_004
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Mark. Yes, I'm on the road. Tonight. It'll be clean.

Name: e1_victor2_005
Text: He hangs up, drops a twenty on the counter for both your coffees, and slides a card across the table: KESSLER RESTRUCTURING — Victor Kessler, Principal.

Name: e1_victor2_006
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: If you ever want work, I hire people who notice things. Drive safe, Mani. The county roads get dark early this time of year.

Name: e1_victor2_007
Text: Only when he's gone do you realise you never told him your name. It was written on your coffee cup.

Name: e1_victor2_008
Text: At the far gas pump, a black car with tinted windows. A man in a long dark coat stands beside it, not pumping gas, facing the restaurant. When you walk out, the car is gone.

Name: e1_main_000
Text: Fog sits on Lake Merrow like something waiting. Three streetlights, sodium orange. A shuttered hardware store. The Merrow Diner, lit and almost empty. St. Brendan's church bell rings six times, though there is no service.

Name: e1_main_001
Text: A bronze plaque at the lakeside: OLD MERROW, 1842–1978. A village given to the water so the valley could prosper.

Name: e1_main_002
Text: Through the diner window, a young woman in an apron sees your car's Windsor plates and waves at you to wait. Across the street, a small brick building with a dark sign: LAKE MERROW 94.1 FM.

Name: e1_station_000
Text: The station is locked. Through the glass door: gold records on the wall, a dark studio, a red ON AIR bulb, unlit. Taped inside the door, a printed notice.

Name: e1_station_001
Text: "AFTER HOURS with Nila is suspended until further notice. — Brian Holt, Station Manager."

Name: e1_station_002
Text: Nila never told you her show was suspended.

Name: e1_ruth_000
Text: The Lakeview's neon sign has two dead letters. Behind the desk, a woman in her sixties, reading glasses on a chain, a police scanner murmuring, a shotgun leaning within easy reach.

Name: e1_ruth_001
Speaker: RUTH
Text: Rooms are forty a night.

Name: e1_ruth_002
Speaker: MANI
Text: I'm Nila's brother. Mani. She lives upstairs.

Name: e1_ruth_003
Text: She looks up slowly. Studies your face like she's checking it against one she knows.

Name: e1_ruth2_000
Speaker: RUTH
Text: You've got her eyes.

Name: e1_ruth2_001
Text: She takes off her glasses.

Name: e1_ruth2_002
Speaker: RUTH
Text: She hasn't been home since Sunday. Her car's in the lot. I called Corbin Monday. Sheriff Corbin. He said she's a grown woman and probably ran off with somebody.

Name: e1_ruth2_003
Text: She slides a key across the counter.

Name: e1_ruth2_004
Speaker: RUTH
Text: Flat's up the back stairs. Tess has the other key. And Mani. I sleep light, and I keep this on all night.

Name: e1_ruth2_005
Text: She taps the scanner.

Name: e1_ruth2b_000
Text: Her face closes like a door.

Name: e1_ruth2b_001
Speaker: RUTH
Text: I don't talk about the sheriff to strangers.

Name: e1_ruth2b_002
Speaker: MANI
Text: I'm not a stranger. I'm her brother.

Name: e1_ruth2b_003
Text: A long pause. She slides a key across the counter without looking at you.

Name: e1_ruth2b_004
Speaker: RUTH
Text: Flat's up the back stairs. She hasn't been home since Sunday. That's all I know.

Name: e1_flat_000
Text: A small two-bedroom. Fairy lights half-strung along the window. A rangoli of coloured chalk on the floor by the door, half-finished, a muddy footprint smudged through it. Posters of old radio stations. A cork board covered in notes.

Name: e1_flat_001
Text: The door bangs open behind you. The young woman from the diner, breathless, still in her apron.

Name: e1_flat_002
Speaker: TESS
Text: You're Mani. She talks about you, like, constantly. "Anna would know what to do."

Name: e1_flat_003
Speaker: TESS
Text: She left Sunday night with her radio bag. She said she'd be back by two. She wasn't.

Name: e1_tess_000
Speaker: TESS
Text: They pulled her show two weeks ago. Brian said "sponsor complaints". The mill's the sponsor. There's a mill? It's been closed my whole life.

Name: e1_tess_001
Speaker: TESS
Text: She got weird after that. Out every night with that radio bag. She said she was "finishing a story". She said, "Tess, if my brother comes, give him the spare key and tell him I'm sorry about Diwali."

Name: e1_tess_002
Text: Tess has to go back for the end of her shift. At the door she hesitates.

Name: e1_tess_003
Speaker: TESS
Text: Lock this. Please.

Name: e1_tess2_000
Text: Tess looks at the boot print. Something passes across her face and is gone.

Name: e1_tess2_001
Speaker: TESS
Text: Lots of guys in this town wear size eleven.

Name: e1_tess2_002
Text: She leaves fast.

Name: e1_cliff_000
Text: You sit in the car to warm up, the gift radio in its wrapping on the passenger seat. Out of habit, you tune the car radio to 94.1, Nila's station. Dead air. A faint hiss.

Name: e1_cliff_001
Text: The dashboard clock turns 23:00.

Name: e1_cliff_002
Text: The hiss shifts. A voice, live, close, tired.

Name: e1_cliff_003
Speaker: NILA
Text: This is After Hours. If anyone's still listening—

Name: e1_cliff_004
Speaker: NILA
Text: Anna, parking-la irukkiradhu nee dhaana? Ennai thedi varaadha. Veetuku po. Please.
Subtitle: Anna, is that you in the lot? Don't come looking for me. Go home. Please.

Name: e1_cliff_005
Speaker: MANI
Text: Nila? NILA!

Name: e1_cliff_006
Text: Silence. Then a second voice on the same frequency. A man. Calm, unhurried, almost kind.

Name: e1_cliff_007
Speaker: MAN'S VOICE
Text: He's already here, Nila.

Name: e1_cliff_008
Text: The signal dies. Far out on the fogged lake, a single red light blinks twice, then goes dark.

Name: e1_end_000
Text: End of Episode 1.

Name: e2_open_000
Text: You stumble out of the car to the edge of the lot and shout her name across the fog. Nothing comes back. Not even an echo.

Name: e2_open_001
Text: Ruth's office light snaps on. She comes out in a cardigan, the scanner in her hand.

Name: e2_open_002
Speaker: RUTH
Text: I heard it. Both voices.

Name: e2_open_003
Speaker: MANI
Text: Where did it come from?

Name: e2_open_004
Speaker: RUTH
Text: Somewhere on the lake. A boat, a cabin, anywhere. (beat) That man's voice. I've heard it before, on the scanner, late. Never says a name. Just listens. And every so often, he answers.

Name: e2_open_005
Text: She looks at you for a long moment.

Name: e2_open_006
Speaker: RUTH
Text: Go upstairs. Lock the door. Don't sleep in the car again.

Name: e2_search_000
Text: You can't sleep. You decide to search the flat properly, the way Nila would. Methodically. Every surface.

Name: e2_laptop_000
Text: The sticky note. Nila always made her passwords into little riddles, so she could tell you over the phone without saying them.

Name: e2_laptop_001
Text: "Appa's shop + the year Anna joined Auragle."

Name: e2_laptop2_000
Text: Her desktop is a mess of folders. Three things stand out.

Name: e2_laptop2_001
Text: An unsent email draft to a journalist in Toronto: "I have callers, photos, and a dive planned. Not just dumping. Something alive is moving through this town."

Name: e2_laptop2_002
Text: An audio folder of After Hours calls. The last file, dated October 20, won't play: "File stored at station."

Name: e2_laptop2_003
Text: And a spreadsheet: Callers.xlsx. Forty-six listener reports, each with a date and an address. Nila never sorted them. You open the town map beside it and start plotting.

Name: e2_laptop3_000
Text: Forty of forty-six dots sit along one line: the lakeshore, and the road up to the closed paper mill.

Name: e2_laptop3_001
Speaker: MANI
Text: Nobody connected them because nobody plotted them.

Name: e2_laptop3_002
Text: Somewhere a floorboard creaks. Then another. Out in the hallway.

Name: e2_hall_000
Text: A flashlight beam slides under the door and stops. A key scrapes in the lock.

Name: e2_hall_001
Speaker: MAN
Text: Ruth said nobody's up here.

Name: e2_hall_closet_000
Text: Through the slats you watch a heavy man in a sheriff's jacket step inside. He doesn't search. He looks at the window where the cable was. Then at the laptop on the desk. He lays his palm on its lid. Still warm.

Name: e2_hall_closet_001
Text: A long pause. You don't breathe.

Name: e2_hall_closet_002
Speaker: SHERIFF
Text: Stubborn family.

Name: e2_hall_closet_003
Text: He leaves, locking the door behind him.

Name: e2_hall_window_000
Text: You drop into the wet grass and press yourself against the wall. Above you, the door opens. A flashlight sweeps the room. A man's shape at the window, looking out at the fog.

Name: e2_hall_window_001
Text: After a long minute, he's gone. You climb back up the drainpipe, shaking.

Name: e2_hall_door_000
Text: A heavy man in a sheriff's jacket fills the doorway. He smiles like a man who has already decided what you are.

Name: e2_hall_door_001
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Sheriff Dale Corbin. And you'd be the brother. Long way from Windsor.

Name: e2_hall_door_002
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Your sister's an adult. Adults leave. I'd start driving early, before the fog gets thick.

Name: e2_hall_door_003
Text: He writes your licence plate in a little notebook and leaves the door open behind him.

Name: e2_diner_000
Text: Vinyl booths, a pie case, and a bulletin board of lost-pet posters. Far too many lost-pet posters. The locals stop talking when you walk in.

Name: e2_diner_001
Text: Tess pours your coffee and slips you extra jam without being asked. Then the kitchen door swings open and a burly man in an apron comes out wiping his hands. He stops dead.

Name: e2_diner_002
Speaker: GUS
Text: Truck stop guy. Small world. Breakfast's on me.

Name: e2_gus_000
Text: Gus refills your coffee. His hand is very steady. His eyes are not.

Name: e2_gus_a_000
Text: Gus spills coffee across the counter. He mops it with a rag for far too long.

Name: e2_gus_a_001
Speaker: GUS
Text: Fine. It was fine.

Name: e2_gus_a_002
Text: He goes back into the kitchen and doesn't come out again.

Name: e2_gus_b_000
Text: Gus relaxes a little.

Name: e2_gus_b_001
Speaker: GUS
Text: Any time. You tell your sister Gus says hi when she turns up. She always tips.

Name: e2_station_000
Text: A small brick station. Gold records from the eighties. A brass plaque at reception: STUDIO RENEWAL 2024 MADE POSSIBLE BY THE HAYDEN FAMILY FOUNDATION.

Name: e2_station_001
Text: The station manager, Brian Holt, polo shirt, too much cologne, meets you in the lobby and tries very hard to keep you there.

Name: e2_station_002
Speaker: BRIAN
Text: Look, I'm sorry about Nila, I am. But her show was suspended for content reasons. She was making accusations on air.

Name: e2_station_003
Speaker: MANI
Text: Accusations against who?

Name: e2_station_004
Speaker: BRIAN
Text: Our sponsor. Merrow Mill Holdings keeps this station alive. Without them we're a guy with a playlist.

Name: e2_brian1_000
Speaker: BRIAN
Text: So, what is it you want?

Name: e2_brian2_000
Speaker: BRIAN
Text: Forty-six? (He swallows.) People call in about all kinds of things.

Name: e2_brian2_001
Speaker: BRIAN
Text: Even if I wanted to help, I can't just let people into the archive.

Name: e2_brian3_000
Text: Brian looks at the front door, then at the clock, then at you.

Name: e2_brian3_001
Speaker: BRIAN
Text: What do you even think is on that tape?

Name: e2_brian_end_000
Text: Brian deflates like a punctured tyre.

Name: e2_brian_end_001
Speaker: BRIAN
Text: Ten minutes. The archive's at the back. If anyone asks, you were fixing the Wi-Fi.

Name: e2_archive_000
Text: A cramped room of shelves. Hundreds of boxed tapes, all with labels in the same format. A laminated note on the wall: "ARCHIVE CODES: AH – year (2 digits) – week of year – show number."

Name: e2_archive_001
Text: On the wall calendar, someone has written week numbers down the side. The week of Mon Oct 19 to Sun Oct 25 is marked "43".

Name: e2_archive_002
Text: You check Nila's radio log page. Her last After Hours: "Tue Oct 20 — show #112."

Name: e2_tape_000
Text: You load the tape. Nila's voice, warm and quick. Then a caller: an old man, whispering.

Name: e2_tape_001
Speaker: CALLER
Text: I won't give my name. My son fishes. In seventy-seven I loaded barrels for the mill, down where the village was, before they flooded it. I was nineteen.

Name: e2_tape_002
Speaker: CALLER
Text: And they're doing it again, miss. Every week. New barrels, new trucks. And the other thing. The animals.

Name: e2_tape_003
Speaker: NILA
Text: Animals?

Name: e2_tape_004
Speaker: CALLER
Text: In crates. Some of them alive. I hear them at night from the dock. Hissing.

Name: e2_tape_005
Speaker: NILA
Text: Listeners, I'm going to the mill myself, and I'll tell you everything I find. Right here, right—

Name: e2_tape_006
Text: A station jingle cuts across her. Brian is in the doorway, rubbing his face.

Name: e2_tape_007
Speaker: BRIAN
Text: I cut the feed. Five minutes later I got a phone call. Not from the mill. From a consultant who'd just signed a two-year sponsorship. Paid in advance.

Name: e2_tape_008
Speaker: BRIAN
Text: Kessler. Victor Kessler.

Name: e2_tape_009
Text: You take Victor's business card from your wallet and look at it for a long time.

Name: e2_lot_000
Text: A sheriff's cruiser is parked across the back of your car. Corbin leans on it, eating a donut from a Tom Portons bag.

Name: e2_lot_001
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Sheriff Dale Corbin. You'd be the brother.

Name: e2_lot_002
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Filing a missing persons report? Good. Come by the station Friday and we'll do it properly.

Name: e2_lot_003
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Today, I'd stay out of folks' business. Folks here are private.

Name: e2_lot_v_000
Text: Corbin's jaw tightens. Just for a second.

Name: e2_lot_v_001
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Never heard of him. (He folds the donut bag very neatly.) Drive safe.

Name: e2_lot_t_000
Text: Corbin goes very quiet. He looks at the station's back door. Then at you.

Name: e2_lot_t_001
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Brian should be more careful with his archive. (He gets into the cruiser.) Drive safe.

Name: e2_lot_p_000
Text: Corbin smiles, satisfied.

Name: e2_lot_p_001
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Good man. (He moves the cruiser.) Friday.

Name: e2_phone_000
Text: Back at the flat. Nila's phone is charged. The lock screen asks for a password. Same riddle-maker, same family.

Name: e2_phone_001
Text: You try the laptop password. Wrong. You think about what Nila would use for herself.

Name: e2_memo_000
Text: The last voice memo, recorded Sunday 23:40. Wind. Water. Nila whispering in the dark.

Name: e2_memo_001
Speaker: NILA
Text: Anna, idha nee kettuttu irundha, naan unkitta nerla solla mudiyala. Eli-ku theriyum. Dock pathi Eli kitta kelu, avan mela kovapadaadha. Tess-ku bayandhu dhaan avan ipdi pannaan.
Subtitle: Anna, if you're hearing this, I couldn't tell you in person. Eli knows. Ask Eli about the dock, and don't be angry with him. He did it because he's scared for Tess.

Name: e2_memo_002
Speaker: NILA
Text: Andha coat potta aal thirumba vandhuttaan. Naan broadcast panra ovvoru raathiriyum avan inga irukkaan. Pakkathula varradhilla. Kettuttu mattum irukkaan.
Subtitle: The man in the coat is back. Every night I broadcast, he's here. He never comes closer. He just listens.

Name: e2_memo_003
Text: A knock at the door.

Name: e2_memo_004
Text: You open it. A broad young man in muddy fisherman's boots, size eleven, eyes red from no sleep.

Name: e2_memo_005
Speaker: ELI
Text: You're her brother. (He looks over his shoulder at the street.) I'm Eli. We need to talk. Not here. Come to the dock.

Name: e2_end_000
Text: End of Episode 2.

Name: e3_open_000
Text: A weathered dock below a clapboard house. Two boats: the family's old trawler, Margaret, and Eli's smaller skiff. Nets, crab traps, a single bulb on a pole.

Name: e3_open_001
Text: Eli doesn't look at you. He talks to the water.

Name: e3_open_002
Speaker: ELI
Text: Sunday night I stood under her window for an hour. I wanted to tell her to stop. To leave. I didn't have the guts to knock.

Name: e3_open_003
Speaker: ELI
Text: Corbin came to our house two weeks ago. He said if I didn't tell him when Nila went out at night, Tess would get arrested for stealing from the diner till. He had a video. It wasn't her. But it looked like her.

Name: e3_open_004
Speaker: ELI
Text: So I told him. I told him she goes out at night with the radio. And three days later she was gone.

Name: e3_bucket_000
Text: Eli leads you to a white bucket behind the crab traps, its lid weighted with a brick.

Name: e3_bucket_001
Speaker: ELI
Text: Found it under the dock Saturday. Nila photographed it. Nobody here knows what it is.

Name: e3_bucket_002
Text: He lifts the lid with a boat hook. Inside, coiled and still: a thick snake, gold and brown, with a broad, arrow-shaped head. It lifts that head toward the light. Its tongue tastes the air.

Name: e3_bucket_003
Text: You pull out your phone and start comparing photos.

Name: e3_snake_000
Text: Golden lancehead. Bothrops insularis. Found in exactly one place on Earth: Ilha da Queimada Grande, "Snake Island", off the coast of Brazil. Critically endangered. Venom several times stronger than its mainland cousins. On the black market, one can sell for tens of thousands of dollars.

Name: e3_snake_001
Speaker: MANI
Text: This isn't from Ontario. Someone brought it here. On purpose.

Name: e3_snake_002
Speaker: ELI
Text: The night boats. Tuesdays and Fridays. They come in to the old mill pier around two in the morning. Dad says he can hear the crates hissing.

Name: e3_snake_003
Text: Something about the way he says "Dad" makes you turn and look up at the house.

Name: e3_dinner_000
Text: A warm, cramped kitchen. Fish stew, fresh bread, a wood stove ticking. Walter Marsh, seventy-two, big scarred hands and a cough he tries to hide in his sleeve. Tess sets the table and squeezes your arm as she passes.

Name: e3_dinner_001
Speaker: WALTER
Text: Eli says you're Nila's brother. She ate at this table every Sunday. Told terrible jokes.

Name: e3_dinner_002
Text: His voice. You've heard it before. On a tape, in a cramped room, whispering about barrels.

Name: e3_walter_000
Text: Walter puts his spoon down. The kitchen goes quiet.

Name: e3_walter_001
Speaker: WALTER
Text: Yes. That was me.

Name: e3_walter_002
Speaker: WALTER
Text: Old Merrow was my village. School, church, my mother's grave. In seventy-seven the mill paid boys fifty dollars a night to roll barrels down into the valley, around the old church, before the dam closed. Said it was safe. Said the water would cover it.

Name: e3_walter_003
Speaker: WALTER
Text: I bought Margaret's wedding ring with that money.

Name: e3_walter_004
Speaker: TESS
Text: Dad.

Name: e3_walter_005
Speaker: WALTER
Text: And now it's happening again. New barrels, every week, same place. But this time it isn't paper waste. It smells like a hospital. And the boats bring crates. Live ones.

Name: e3_house_000
Text: After dinner, Walter falls asleep in his chair. Eli washes dishes. You look around.

Name: e3_map_000
Text: Eli brings a shoebox from under his bed.

Name: e3_map_001
Speaker: ELI
Text: Nila left this on my boat. When she disappeared I tore it up. I don't know why. I couldn't look at it. Then I couldn't throw it away.

Name: e3_map_002
Text: Pieces of a hand-drawn map. Nila's handwriting. Street names. You lay Walter's photo of Old Merrow beside them and match each piece, from the shore up to the church.

Name: e3_map2_000
Text: The map is whole. Three marks in Nila's red pen.

Name: e3_map2_001
Text: An X on the drowned church: "barrels — dive here".

Name: e3_map2_002
Text: The old mill pier, Pier 3: "boats Tue/Fri 02:00".

Name: e3_map2_003
Text: And at the far end of the lake, a little tower symbol on a headland: "PP. Jonah. Safe."

Name: e3_map2_004
Speaker: MANI
Text: PP. It's in her radio log. Every night. PP.

Name: e3_map2_005
Speaker: ELI
Text: Pike Point. There's an old radio tower out there. Nobody goes out there except a crazy old guy. Jonah Pike.

Name: e3_porch_000
Text: Tess walks you to the porch. Wind off the lake. She hugs herself.

Name: e3_porch_001
Speaker: TESS
Text: Everybody here's waiting for something to come up out of that lake. Me, I'm just waiting for a bus.

Name: e3_porch_002
Speaker: TESS
Text: Corbin came by the diner again today. He asked if I'd seen "the brother".

Name: e3_porch_a_000
Text: Tess looks at you for a long time. Then she nods once, like she's decided to believe it.

Name: e3_porch_a_001
Speaker: TESS
Text: Okay. (beat) Okay.

Name: e3_porch_a_002
Text: Behind the screen door, Eli has heard every word.

Name: e3_porch_b_000
Speaker: TESS
Text: He asked if Nila ever talked about Pike Point. I said no. That was a lie. She talked about it all the time.

Name: e3_porch_b_001
Text: So the villains already suspect where Nila is.

Name: e3_boat_000
Text: Eli rows you out with the engine off. Fog as thick as milk. You can't see the bow of the boat. St. Brendan's bell tolls the half hour from the shore.

Name: e3_boat_001
Speaker: ELI
Text: Pier 3 is northeast of the church bell. Steer by the sound. Keep it over your left shoulder.

Name: e3_boat_002
Text: The bell rings. It sounds like it's coming from behind you, slightly to the right.

Name: e3_boat_wrong_000
Text: A hollow knock under the hull. The boat lurches. Eli flinches and grabs the gunwale.

Name: e3_boat_wrong_001
Speaker: ELI
Text: Rooftop. The old village. We're right over it.

Name: e3_boat_wrong_002
Text: Somewhere beneath you, a drowned house. You hold your breath until the boat slides free. The bell rings again; this time you keep it over your left shoulder.

Name: e3_pier_000
Text: Floodlights through the fog. An unmarked boat ties up at the old mill pier. Men pass crates up a ramp. Some crates have air holes and are stencilled LIVE BAIT — KEEP WARM. Blue barrels roll the other way, down onto the boat.

Name: e3_pier_001
Text: A man in a tailored wool coat supervises with a coffee cup. Victor.

Name: e3_light_000
Text: A searchlight swings across the water toward the skiff.

Name: e3_light_a_000
Text: You press your faces into the wet planks. The light passes over the boat like a hand. It doesn't stop. Eli exhales.

Name: e3_light_b_000
Text: The oars splash. The light swings back and finds your wake. A shout from the pier. Then the fog closes and you're gone.

Name: e3_light_c_000
Text: The light lands full on the skiff. For one long second you are lit up like a stage. Victor lowers his coffee cup. Then the fog rolls between you.

Name: e3_fire_000
Text: Orange light through the fog before you can see the dock. Margaret, the family trawler, is on fire. Walter is on the dock in his undershirt with a garden hose. Tess is screaming for help.

Name: e3_fire_001
Text: Eli jumps onto the dock and runs to his father. You reach the white bucket behind the crab traps.

Name: e3_fire_002
Text: The lid is off. The bucket is empty.

Name: e3_fire_003
Text: On the post beside it, pinned with a fishing knife: a photo of Tess serving coffee at the diner, taken through the window. On the back, in neat handwriting:

Name: e3_fire_004
Text: "Bait."

Name: e3_fire_005
Text: On the road above, a sheriff's cruiser rolls slowly away with its lights off.

Name: e3_end_000
Text: End of Episode 3.

Name: e4_open_000
Text: Dawn. Margaret is a blackened hull. Walter sits on an upturned crate, coughing into his fist. Sheriff Corbin walks the dock, hands in his pockets.

Name: e4_open_001
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Electrical fault. Old boat, old wiring. Happens.

Name: e4_open_002
Speaker: ELI
Text: Somebody pinned a photo of my sister to that post.

Name: e4_open_003
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Kids. (He looks at you.) Trouble does seem to follow strangers around, doesn't it.

Name: e4_open_a_000
Text: Corbin takes the knife and photo in a plastic bag.

Name: e4_open_a_001
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Evidence. I'll look into it.

Name: e4_open_a_002
Text: You will never see either of them again.

Name: e4_open_b_000
Text: You say nothing. The knife is a cold weight against your ribs. Corbin watches you a beat too long, then walks away whistling.

Name: e4_interview_000
Text: Your phone alarm: "Interview — Data Analytics Engineer, Round 2, 11:00." You'd forgotten. Completely.

Name: e4_interview_001
Text: Ruth lets you use the office. Behind your laptop camera: her scanner, the shotgun, a stuffed pike on the wall. You turn the laptop so the pike is out of frame.

Name: e4_interview_002
Speaker: DEBORAH
Text: Thanks for joining, Mani. Let's start. Tell us about a time you found a pattern nobody else noticed.

Name: e4_int2_000
Speaker: DEBORAH
Text: How do you handle working with incomplete or messy data?

Name: e4_int3_000
Text: Ruth's scanner crackles behind you. Deborah's eyebrows go up.

Name: e4_int3_001
Speaker: DEBORAH
Text: Last one. Why do you want this job?

Name: e4_int_end_000
Text: Deborah smiles for the first time. "That's a great answer. We'll be in touch very soon."

Name: e4_int_end_001
Text: You close the laptop. Ruth is watching you from the doorway.

Name: e4_int_end_002
Speaker: RUTH
Text: You're going to that mill, aren't you.

Name: e4_ruth_000
Text: Ruth hesitates. Then she takes one spiral notebook out of a drawer and drops it on the desk.

Name: e4_ruth_001
Speaker: RUTH
Text: This year's. Trucks up the mill road. Date, time, plate. Don't ask me why I keep it.

Name: e4_ruth_p1_000
Text: You spread the notebook pages across the desk and do what you do best. Sort by day. Sort by hour. Count.

Name: e4_ruth_p2_000
Text: The same nights as the boats. In the margins, Ruth has scribbled scanner notes. You read them down the page.

Name: e4_ruth_p2_001
Text: "Mill security, 23:40: 'Shift change, cams going to reset.' 23:52: 'Cams back up.'" Every night, the same.

Name: e4_ruth_p2_002
Text: Twelve minutes, every night, when the yard cameras are blind.

Name: e4_ruth_end_000
Speaker: MANI
Text: Tonight. 23:40. North fence.

Name: e4_ruth_end_001
Speaker: RUTH
Text: You're going in there. (It isn't a question.) Then take these.

Name: e4_ruth_end_002
Text: A heavy flashlight and a pair of bolt cutters.

Name: e4_ruth_end_003
Speaker: RUTH
Text: Not the shotgun. You'd shoot your own foot.

Name: e4_fence_000
Text: Merrow Paper Mill. Brick sheds, a smokestack, broken windows. But warm light leaks from the pulping hall, and steam rises from the boiler house. A sign: CLOSED 2009. PRIVATE PROPERTY.

Name: e4_fence_001
Text: 23:40. The camera on the fence post stops blinking. Twelve minutes.

Name: e4_fence_002
Text: You cut the fence. Ahead, the yard: a gravel path straight to the pulping hall, or the long way round through the dead grass.

Name: e4_fence2_000
Text: A guard's flashlight swings along the wall toward you. Behind you, a stack of pallets. To your left, an open shed door.

Name: e4_hall_000
Text: The paper machines are gone. In their place: plastic sheeting, ventilation fans, a long steel table. Three workers in respirators feed powder into two pill presses that thump out small blue tablets stamped M30.

Name: e4_hall_001
Text: Counterfeit oxycodone. Which means fentanyl.

Name: e4_hall_002
Text: Blue barrels of chemical sludge stand by the loading door, waiting.

Name: e4_pills_000
Text: A sealed bag of pills sits on the end of the table, a metre from the nearest worker's back. Physical evidence. If you can reach it.

Name: e4_pills_try_000
Text: You crouch. The worker shifts his weight. The press thumps.

Name: e4_pills_ok_000
Text: Your hand closes on the bag between one thump and the next. You're back in the shadows before the press lands again.

Name: e4_pills_seen_000
Text: The worker turns. Your eyes meet over his respirator. He opens his mouth. You run, and he hesitates just long enough. You don't get the bag.

Name: e4_boiler_000
Text: Heat hits like a wall. Humid, green, almost beautiful. Rows of glass tanks under heat lamps.

Name: e4_boiler_001
Text: Tiny poison dart frogs, bright blue and yellow. Radiated tortoises from Madagascar stacked in crates. Slow lorises in small cages, blinking. And at the far end, a locked glass vault with a brass plate: B. INSULARIS — ILHA DA QUEIMADA GRANDE — 6.

Name: e4_boiler_002
Text: Only five snakes inside. The one from Eli's bucket came from here. Someone took it back.

Name: e4_boiler_003
Text: You step back and your shoulder catches a heat-lamp cable. The lights flicker, buzz, and die. In the dark, somewhere close, a tank latch clicks.

Name: e4_snake1_000
Text: Your flashlight finds it: gold coils on the floor, a metre in front of your boots, head lifting.

Name: e4_snake2_000
Text: It slides past your boot. It's behind you now, between you and the door. A pipe runs along the floor to your right.

Name: e4_snake3_000
Text: It rises. Its head sways at knee height, tasting the heat of you.

Name: e4_snake_end_000
Text: You back out of the boiler house one slow step at a time. The snake loses interest and coils under a tank.

Name: e4_snake_end_001
Text: Behind you, a worker swears in the dark: "Which idiot left the lamp off?"

Name: e4_keypad_000
Text: The old mill manager's office, upstairs. A keypad on the door. Beside it, a framed Diwali card, of all things, signed "V.K. — every lock should remember the day it all began."

Name: e4_keypad_001
Text: Next to it, a framed newspaper clipping: "KESSLER RESTRUCTURING TAKES OVER MERROW MILL HOLDINGS — signed March 14, 2019."

Name: e4_keypad_002
Text: Four digits.

Name: e4_office_000
Text: Leather chairs, whisky, a hotel-suite carpet. On the desk, a large glass terrarium with one golden lancehead, bigger than the rest. A brass tag: MIDAS.

Name: e4_office_001
Text: Victor's laptop is open. A spreadsheet.

Name: e4_overhear_000
Text: Footsteps on the stairs. You duck behind the terrarium. Victor comes in with Corbin, mid-conversation.

Name: e4_overhear_001
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: …and I don't care what he looks like, Dale. He's a nice boy from Windsor with a box of sweets. Nice boys go home if you ask them correctly.

Name: e4_overhear_002
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: And the sister?

Name: e4_overhear_003
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Hades wants her found before she broadcasts again. She knows his voice. Nobody knows his voice.

Name: e4_overhear_004
Text: He taps the terrarium. Midas rises.

Name: e4_overhear_005
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Find her, Dale. Or I find a use for you.

Name: e4_overhear_006
Text: Corbin leaves. Victor pours a whisky and talks to the snake.

Name: e4_overhear_007
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Festival of lights, Midas. Good triumphs over evil. (He laughs.) Every year, they still believe it.

Name: e4_chase_000
Text: An alarm whoops. The camera reset is over. A guard with a shotgun sees you at the office window.

Name: e4_chase_001
Speaker: GUARD
Text: HEY!

Name: e4_chase_002
Text: The window beside your head explodes. You run.

Name: e4_ch1_000
Text: Down from the office: a catwalk across the hall, or the stairs to the yard.

Name: e4_ch2_000
Text: Two men ahead. Cover: a row of barrels, or a parked truck.

Name: e4_ch3_000
Text: A conveyor belt blocks the way. Over it or under it?

Name: e4_ch4_000
Text: The fence, ten metres. Or the outflow ditch beside it.

Name: e4_ch_end_000
Text: You're through the fence and into the trees before the first guard reaches the yard. Flashlights sweep the woods behind you, too late.

Name: e4_ditch_000
Text: You lie in a ditch of freezing water, heart hammering, the USB stick clenched in your fist. A refrigerated truck rumbles past: MERROW PALLETS & SUPPLY. The cab light flicks on.

Name: e4_ditch_001
Text: The driver is Gus Pell, still in his diner apron, humming.

Name: e4_ditch_002
Text: Your phone buzzes. Unknown number. You answer and say nothing.

Name: e4_ditch_003
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: You left your coffee cup at my truck stop, Mani. And your footprints all over my boiler house.

Name: e4_ditch_004
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: You've got her eyes. Did anyone tell you that? Same stubborn eyes.

Name: e4_ditch_005
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Here's my last offer. Go home. Light your lamps. Call your mother. Or I start taking the people you've met here. One at a time. Until you do.

Name: e4_ditch_006
Text: The line goes dead. On the hill, the red light on the water tower blinks twice.

Name: e4_end_000
Text: End of Episode 4.

Name: e5_open_000
Text: You wake on the couch. Your palms are torn from the fence wire and one cut on your hand won't stop bleeding through the tissue.

Name: e5_open_001
Text: Tess, getting ready for her shift, sees the blood on the cushion and drops her mug.

Name: e5_open_002
Speaker: TESS
Text: That needs stitches. We're going to Dr. Rao. Now.

Name: e5_clinic_000
Text: A small clinic with faded flu-shot posters. Dr. Anika Rao, forty-six, sharp, exhausted, examines you with gloved hands.

Name: e5_clinic_001
Speaker: DR. RAO
Text: Four stitches. Wire, not glass. (beat) There's only one fence in this town with wire like that. You've been up at the mill.

Name: e5_clinic_002
Speaker: MANI
Text: There's a lab up there. And a room full of animals. Golden lanceheads, from Brazil.

Name: e5_clinic_003
Text: She stops wrapping the bandage.

Name: e5_clinic_004
Speaker: DR. RAO
Text: I don't know anything about that. Keep it clean. Come back if it blackens.

Name: e5_rao1_000
Text: She's already turning away. You have one chance to make her listen.

Name: e5_rao2_000
Speaker: DR. RAO
Text: (very quietly) I have that map. I drew it myself in 2015. Nobody wanted it.

Name: e5_rao2_001
Text: She folds her arms.

Name: e5_rao3_000
Text: Dr. Rao goes white.

Name: e5_rao3_001
Speaker: DR. RAO
Text: Four overdoses since spring. Young people. I was told to sign them as heart failure.

Name: e5_rao3_002
Speaker: MANI
Text: Told by whom?

Name: e5_rao3_003
Speaker: DR. RAO
Text: The county coroner. Who is also our sheriff.

Name: e5_rao3_004
Text: She turns her back to you, very deliberately, and puts a small brass key on the counter beside the sink.

Name: e5_rao3_005
Speaker: DR. RAO
Text: I go to lunch at one. The back door sticks. Everyone knows that.

Name: e5_station_000
Text: Wood panelling, burnt coffee, a wall of framed photos. Corbin with the mayor. Corbin at a fish fry. Corbin shaking hands at a ribbon cutting, captioned "Mill Holdings partners, 2019". Victor, younger, smiling in the background.

Name: e5_station_001
Text: At a side desk, a young deputy types slowly, watching everything. His name plate says S. ORTIZ.

Name: e5_station_002
Text: You're here to file a missing persons report. Corbin takes it personally.

Name: e5_station_003
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Your sister had a gift for stirring things up. People here don't like being stirred.

Name: e5_cb1_000
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: When did you last speak to her?

Name: e5_cb2_000
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: And what have you been doing in town all week?

Name: e5_cb3_000
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: (writing nothing down) Anything else? Anything you've seen?

Name: e5_cb_end_000
Text: Corbin relaxes, almost bored with you.

Name: e5_cb_end_001
Text: His radio squawks. He steps into the back room. His desk drawer is open about an inch.

Name: e5_drawer_000
Text: A thick envelope of cash, rubber-banded, with a sticky note: "Nov — V." Under it, a folder: Coroner's reports — Greyhaven, 2026. Four death certificates, all signed "cardiac arrest".

Name: e5_drawer_001
Text: Three seconds. Three photos. You're back in your chair when Corbin comes out.

Name: e5_stay_000
Text: You stay put. Corbin comes back, hands you a form, and watches you fill it in. Across the room, Deputy Ortiz is watching too. Watching the drawer.

Name: e5_ortiz_000
Text: Ortiz walks you to your car. Out of Corbin's earshot, he speaks without turning his head.

Name: e5_ortiz_001
Speaker: ORTIZ
Text: Did your sister ever say my name?

Name: e5_ortiz2_000
Speaker: ORTIZ
Text: I didn't sign up to be anybody's dog. (beat) Two of those kids who died, I went to school with their brothers.

Name: e5_ortiz2_001
Text: He glances at the station.

Name: e5_ortiz2_002
Speaker: ORTIZ
Text: The men at that mill carry rifles, Mani. You don't.

Name: e5_ortiz2_003
Text: He opens his trunk and hands you a small revolver wrapped in a cloth.

Name: e5_ortiz2_004
Speaker: ORTIZ
Text: Confiscated off a poacher last year. It's not in any system. I didn't give you this.

Name: e5_range_000
Text: Behind the old gravel pit, Ortiz sets three cans on a log.

Name: e5_range_001
Speaker: ORTIZ
Text: Six rounds. Every one counts. Show me how you'd do it.

Name: e5_range2_000
Text: You miss the first can. You miss the second. The third jumps off the log. The sound is enormous. Your ears ring and your hands shake.

Name: e5_range2_001
Speaker: MANI
Text: I write code, man.

Name: e5_range2_002
Speaker: ORTIZ
Text: Then think of it as the last line. You hope you never reach it.

Name: e5_gus_000
Text: Gus is smoking by the dumpsters. You step out of the shadow behind him and hold up your phone: the ledger. "G.P. — runs, $1,200 per run."

Name: e5_gus_001
Text: Gus drops the cigarette.

Name: e5_gus_002
Speaker: GUS
Text: The diner's been losing money for nine years. My wife's chemo wasn't covered. Victor came in with an envelope.

Name: e5_gus_003
Speaker: GUS
Text: I drive. That's all. I don't look in the back.

Name: e5_gus_a_000
Text: Gus panics. He talks fast, too fast, to make you go away.

Name: e5_gus_a_001
Speaker: GUS
Text: Saturday. Tomorrow night. The last run. Victor's shutting it all down. The lab, the animals, everything into the lake. Then he burns the mill.

Name: e5_gus_a_002
Text: He goes back inside. Through the window, you see him pick up the phone.

Name: e5_gus_b_000
Text: Gus looks at you for a long time. Then he sits down on an upturned milk crate.

Name: e5_gus_b_001
Speaker: GUS
Text: Saturday night. Tomorrow. The last run. Victor's shutting it all down: the lab, the animals, everything into the lake. Then he burns the mill for the insurance. He wants it clean before the partner comes to look.

Name: e5_gus_b_002
Speaker: MANI
Text: Hades.

Name: e5_gus_b_003
Speaker: GUS
Text: I've never seen him. Nobody has. Victor calls him Mark when he's drunk. Just Mark.

Name: e5_gus_b_004
Speaker: GUS
Text: If you need a truck, or a road, or a door left open, you call me.

Name: e5_records_000
Text: The back door sticks, exactly as promised. A narrow room of filing cabinets and boxes going back to 1979. Thirty years of a town's bodies, on paper.

Name: e5_records_001
Text: You do what you know. You treat it like a dataset.

Name: e5_records2_000
Text: Now the four 2026 "cardiac" deaths. You line up their dates against Ruth's truck log.

Name: e5_records3_000
Text: Clipped to the last file, in Dr. Rao's handwriting: "Not cardiac. Fentanyl. Signed under protest. A.R."

Name: e5_records3_001
Text: You photograph everything. Thirty years. Four kids. One road.

Name: e5_motel_000
Text: Dusk. The motel sign is dark. The office door is open.

Name: e5_motel_001
Text: Inside: drawers on the floor. The stuffed pike smashed. Ruth's scanner stamped flat on the tiles, still hissing. Her chair tipped over. The shotgun gone.

Name: e5_motel_002
Text: The floorboard behind the desk is still in place. You lift it. Fourteen notebooks, untouched. She hid them before they came.

Name: e5_motel_003
Text: On the counter, set neatly in the middle of the mess: Victor's business card. On the back, in the same neat hand as the note on the Marsh dock:

Name: e5_motel_004
Text: "One at a time."

Name: e5_motel_005
Text: Outside, your car sits on four slashed tyres. Out on the lake, the church bell rings six. Then, a seventh time. It never does that.

Name: e5_end_000
Text: End of Episode 5.

Name: e6_open_000
Text: You, Eli and Ortiz, off duty in a hoodie, have searched the lakeshore for Ruth for four hours. Her skiff is gone from its mooring. That's all you found.

Name: e6_open_001
Text: Ortiz leaves to cover his night shift so Corbin won't suspect him. Eli falls asleep in a chair, boots still on.

Name: e6_open_002
Text: Your phone lights up. Amma, video call. It's Saturday morning in Vellore. Behind her, oil lamps lined up on the windowsill. Appa is hanging a string of mango leaves over the door.

Name: e6_open_003
Speaker: AMMA
Text: Kanna! Naalaiku Deepavali. Nila-va kooppidu, rendu pasangalaiyum onna paakkanum.
Subtitle: Kanna! Tomorrow is Deepavali. Call Nila over, I want to see both my children together.

Name: e6_truth_000
Text: Amma's face crumples. She puts her hand over her mouth. Appa takes the phone from her, and his voice is steady.

Name: e6_truth_001
Speaker: APPA
Text: Appo kandupidi, kanna. Naanga vilakku yethi kaathirukkom.
Subtitle: Then find her, kanna. We'll light the lamps and wait.

Name: e6_truth_002
Speaker: APPA
Text: Mani. Airport-la unna anuppa vandhappo nee sonna, "Naan avala paathukuren, Appa." Naan oru naalum sandhegapattadhilla.
Subtitle: Mani. When we came to see you off at the airport, you said, "I'll look after her, Appa." I have never doubted it.

Name: e6_lie_000
Text: Amma beams. She tells you what she's cooking. She tells you to make Nila wear the green silk. You say yes to everything.

Name: e6_lie_001
Speaker: APPA
Text: Mani. Airport-la unna anuppa vandhappo nee sonna, "Naan avala paathukuren, Appa." Naan oru naalum sandhegapattadhilla.
Subtitle: Mani. When we came to see you off at the airport, you said, "I'll look after her, Appa." I have never doubted it.

Name: e6_lie_002
Text: The call ends. You sit alone in the dark flat with the lie, and it is very heavy.

Name: e6_church_000
Text: A small stone church on the hill, lit by candles. The bell rope hangs in a corner. An old priest pulls it for seven o'clock, slowly, exactly seven times.

Name: e6_church_001
Speaker: MANI
Text: Last night it rang seven at six o'clock.

Name: e6_church_002
Speaker: FATHER REID
Text: It did. Ruth Vane and I have an arrangement, from years ago, when she first started writing down trucks. If anyone ever came for her, I was to ring once more than the hour.

Name: e6_church_003
Speaker: FATHER REID
Text: It means she got away. It means she's safe.

Name: e6_church_004
Speaker: MANI
Text: Where?

Name: e6_church_005
Speaker: FATHER REID
Text: She didn't tell me, so no one could make me tell them. But she left a message, if you came asking. (He reads from a folded paper.) "Get the camera from the church. It's what Nila went back for. Then the water will bring you to me."

Name: e6_church_006
Speaker: MANI
Text: This church?

Name: e6_church_007
Speaker: FATHER REID
Text: No, son. The other one. The one underneath the lake.

Name: e6_archive_000
Text: Rows of boxes. Parish records. Photographs of Old Merrow: a schoolhouse, a general store, a stone church with a tall spire, families in Sunday clothes.

Name: e6_archive_001
Speaker: FATHER REID
Text: I was born down there. Baptised in that church. When they flooded the valley, they promised us the water would be clean. They moved our dead up the hill. (beat) Not all of them.

Name: e6_walter_000
Text: You show Walter the 1977 photo. He looks at it for a long time.

Name: e6_walter_001
Speaker: WALTER
Text: Fifty dollars a night. I bought Margaret's ring with it. I've been paying for that ring my whole life.

Name: e6_walter_002
Speaker: WALTER
Text: I told Father Tom, in confession, forty years ago. He never told a soul. (He stands.) My old diving gear's in the shed. The hose is good. I'll run the compressor myself. Eli steers.

Name: e6_prep_000
Text: Walter's old aluminium workboat. A small petrol compressor chugging on deck. A long yellow air hose. The fog is lifting into a grey, cold day.

Name: e6_prep_001
Text: You're in Walter's ancient wetsuit, a mask, a waterproof flashlight, Nila's map sealed in a plastic sleeve on your wrist. Your phone in a waterproof pouch.

Name: e6_prep_002
Speaker: ELI
Text: Three tugs on the line means pull you up. You tug three times, we pull. Don't be a hero.

Name: e6_prep_003
Text: You roll backward off the side.

Name: e6_dive_000
Text: Green darkness. Then shapes. A drowned village, perfectly still.

Name: e6_dive_001
Text: Your breath roars in your ears. The yellow hose trails up behind you to a pale disc of light.

Name: e6_church_in_000
Text: You swim through the open doors of the church. Pews in rows. A fallen cross. A stained-glass window glowing faintly green. Barrels stacked to the rafters down the aisles.

Name: e6_church_in_001
Text: In the front pew, wedged under the kneeler, where she must have dropped it when her own air ran low: a yellow dive-camera housing. NILA, in marker on the strap.

Name: e6_church_in_002
Text: You pull it free. A barrel shifts above you. Then another. A slow avalanche of steel. Silt explodes into the water and the light goes brown.

Name: e6_silt1_000
Text: Brown nothing. Your flashlight shows only your own hand. Then, faintly: clank. Clank. Clank. Walter, tapping a wrench on the hull above. Louder to your left.

Name: e6_silt1_001
Text: You try to remember which way you came in.

Name: e6_silt_bad_000
Text: Barrels. A wall of barrels where the doors were. The avalanche has blocked the main entrance. You turn back.

Name: e6_silt_bad_001
Text: The tapping, to your left.

Name: e6_silt_bad2_000
Text: Your hand finds stone steps going down. The crypt. Absolutely not. You turn around, heart slamming.

Name: e6_silt_bad2_001
Text: The tapping, to your left.

Name: e6_silt2_000
Text: Your glove finds a wooden door frame. A narrow doorway. Above it, the silt is thinner, and there's grey light.

Name: e6_silt3_000
Text: The wall goes on. The tapping is directly above the doorway you just passed. You go back.

Name: e6_ascend_000
Text: You rise through the drowned bell tower. Daylight above, a pale disc. The shadow of Walter's boat. And beside it, a second hull: longer, darker, an outboard idling.

Name: e6_ascend_001
Text: You draw a breath from the regulator. Air comes. Then half a breath. Then nothing.

Name: e6_ascend_002
Text: You look up. The yellow air hose drifts down past your face, cut clean. On the surface, a gloved hand pulls back into the second boat. A blade flashes.

Name: e6_ascend_003
Text: You tug three times on the hose. It comes down limp into your hands.

Name: e6_ascend_004
Text: Four metres to the surface. Your lungs burn. The light gets further away.

Name: e6_end_000
Text: End of Episode 6.

Name: e7_open_000
Text: Black. A muffled boom through the water: a shotgun. Then a hand grabs your harness and hauls you upward. Eli, who dived in after you without a mask.

Name: e7_open_001
Text: You break the surface choking. A small skiff roars out of the fog. Standing in it, soaked, grey hair loose, shotgun at her shoulder: Ruth Vane. She fires again over the second boat. Its outboard screams and it flees into the fog.

Name: e7_open_002
Speaker: RUTH
Text: Told you I sleep light.

Name: e7_open_003
Text: Walter, shaking, wraps you in a blanket. You check the yellow housing in your arms. Nila's camera is safe.

Name: e7_skiff_000
Text: Ruth steers north toward a dark wooded headland. An old steel radio tower rises out of the trees. Pike Point.

Name: e7_skiff_001
Speaker: RUTH
Text: They came Thursday night. Two of them. I went out the back with Harold's shotgun and took the skiff. I've been at Jonah Pike's cabin since.

Name: e7_skiff_002
Speaker: RUTH
Text: Nila told me once: "If I'm not home, I'm with Jonah." Jonah won't tell even me where she is. Stubborn old goat.

Name: e7_skiff_003
Speaker: MANI
Text: Is she—

Name: e7_skiff_004
Speaker: RUTH
Text: He says she's alive. He says it every day. I choose to believe him.

Name: e7_jonah_000
Text: A log cabin crammed with radios: shortwave sets, oscilloscopes, a wall of QSL cards from around the world. Jonah Pike, seventy, white beard, a cardigan full of holes, looks at you over his glasses for a long time.

Name: e7_jonah_001
Speaker: JONAH
Text: You're Anna. She talks about you on the air when she thinks nobody's listening. (beat) Somebody always was.

Name: e7_jonah_002
Text: He's recorded every one of Nila's 23:00 broadcasts. And something else.

Name: e7_footage_000
Text: You connect Nila's camera to Jonah's monitor. Timestamped last Sunday, 22:10.

Name: e7_footage_001
Text: Underwater: the barrels, the dead tortoises, a milky cloud. Then Nila surfaces under a dock and films the boat above it. Victor and Corbin, side by side, watching workers drop a crate over the side.

Name: e7_footage_002
Speaker: CORBIN
Text: Is that the last of the dead ones?

Name: e7_footage_003
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: The ones Hades won't pay for, yes.

Name: e7_footage_004
Text: The camera turns to Nila's face, lit by her dive torch, whispering:

Name: e7_footage_005
Speaker: NILA
Text: If someone's watching this, I didn't make it back. Barrels at St. Brendan's. Victor Kessler. Sheriff Corbin. Tell everyone.

Name: e7_footage_006
Speaker: MANI
Text: She made it back. (To Jonah.) Take me to her.

Name: e7_trail_000
Text: Jonah leads you and Ruth up a rough path through the pines. Wind off the lake. Above, the rusted tower, a single red aircraft light still blinking at the top.

Name: e7_trail_001
Speaker: JONAH
Text: That was 94.1's original transmitter, till they moved it into town in '98. They left everything. I kept it alive, out of spite. (beat) It still reaches every radio in the county.

Name: e7_trail_002
Speaker: MANI
Text: That's how she broadcast on 94.1 when the station was off.

Name: e7_trail_003
Speaker: JONAH
Text: Watch your feet. She's rigged the trail. Trip wires, tin cans, a flare.

Name: e7_trip1_000
Text: Your flashlight catches a glint at ankle height between two pines. Or was it just ice?

Name: e7_trip2_000
Text: A fallen log across the path. The obvious step is right in the middle.

Name: e7_trip3_000
Text: The shed is in sight. A string of fishing line runs low across the last metre, tied to a flare stake.

Name: e7_trip_end_000
Text: You reach the shed without a sound. Jonah nods, impressed.

Name: e7_reunion_000
Text: A concrete shed at the foot of the tower. A camp stove, a sleeping bag, tins of beans, a crate of bottled spring water (half empty), a rack of humming transmitter equipment. Nila's radio bag on a hook.

Name: e7_reunion_001
Speaker: NILA
Text: Stop right there.

Name: e7_reunion_002
Text: She steps from behind the transmitter rack with a flare gun in a shaking hand. Thinner. Hair tied back. A scrape across one cheek.

Name: e7_reunion_003
Text: She sees your face. The flare gun drops.

Name: e7_reunion_004
Speaker: NILA
Text: Anna?

Name: e7_reunion_005
Text: For a long moment, neither of you moves. Then she's across the shed and you're holding her, and she's crying and laughing and hitting your shoulder.

Name: e7_reunion_006
Speaker: NILA
Text: Naan dhaan vara vendaamnu sonnene!
Subtitle: I told you not to come!

Name: e7_reunion_007
Speaker: MANI
Text: Eppo naan un pechu kettirukken?
Subtitle: Since when do I listen to you?

Name: e7_talk_000
Text: Ruth and Jonah step outside to give you a minute. You sit on the sleeping bag together.

Name: e7_talk_001
Text: There's so much to say. Where do you start?

Name: e7_t1_000
Speaker: NILA
Text: Amma-ku theriyuma?
Subtitle: Does Amma know?

Name: e7_t1_001
Speaker: MANI
Text: Illa. Nee kulichittu irukkannu sonnen.
Subtitle: No. I told her you were having a bath.

Name: e7_t1_002
Text: Nila laughs, then stops laughing.

Name: e7_t1_003
Speaker: NILA
Text: Naalaiku naane solren.
Subtitle: I'll tell her myself tomorrow.

Name: e7_t2_000
Speaker: NILA
Text: Corbin's car outside the flat. Men on the stairs. I went out the back with my radio bag, along the shore in the dark, all the way to Jonah's.

Name: e7_t2_001
Speaker: NILA
Text: Phone-a vittutu odinen. Rangoli-a paadhi-la vittutten. Kaalaila thirumbi varuvennu nenachen.
Subtitle: I ran and left my phone. I left my rangoli half done. I thought I'd be back by morning.

Name: e7_t3_000
Text: Nila goes quiet.

Name: e7_t3_001
Speaker: NILA
Text: Avan enakku badhil sonnaan. Ovvoru raathiriyum. Naan enna dress pottirukkennu avanukku theriyum. Naan azhudhadhu kooda theriyum. Water tower-ai vida pakkathula naan avana paathadhe illa.
Subtitle: He answered me. Every night. He knew what I was wearing. He even knew when I cried. I never saw him closer than the water tower.

Name: e7_t4_000
Speaker: NILA
Text: Naan night-la veliya poradha avan Corbin kitta sonnaan. Enakku theriyum. Avan mela kovapadaadha. Corbin Tess vaazhkaiya azhichiruppaan.
Subtitle: He told Corbin I went out at night. I know. Don't be angry with him. Corbin would have destroyed Tess's life.

Name: e7_gift_000
Text: You pull a gift-wrapped box out of your soaked duffel. The bow is crushed.

Name: e7_gift_001
Speaker: MANI
Text: Happy Deepavali. Oru naal munnaadiye.
Subtitle: Happy Deepavali. A day early.

Name: e7_gift_002
Text: She unwraps it. A new handheld ham radio. She laughs through tears.

Name: e7_gift_003
Speaker: NILA
Text: Oru crime scene vazhiya naalu mani neram drive panni enakku radio kondu vandhiya?
Subtitle: You drove four hours through a crime scene to bring me a radio?

Name: e7_gift_004
Speaker: MANI
Text: Sweets-um dhaan. Konjam nanaanjiduchu.
Subtitle: And sweets. They got a bit wet.

Name: e7_plan_000
Text: The four of you around the camp stove, the proof spread on the concrete floor.

Name: e7_plan_001
Text: Jonah nudges the crate of water bottles with his boot.

Name: e7_plan_002
Speaker: JONAH
Text: Where'd these come from? I never brought you water.

Name: e7_plan_003
Speaker: NILA
Text: They were here when I came. I thought you left them.

Name: e7_plan_004
Text: Jonah frowns. Then the plan takes over, and nobody mentions it again.

Name: e7_plan_005
Speaker: NILA
Text: There's no cell signal on Pike Point. If we drive out to call the police, Corbin's on every road. If we call 911 from town, it routes through Corbin's dispatch.

Name: e7_plan_006
Speaker: JONAH
Text: So you don't call. You broadcast.

Name: e7_plan_007
Speaker: NILA
Text: At 23:00. On 94.1, to every radio in the county. On 7.185 for the ham operators. And Jonah patches it onto the provincial police band. (beat) They can bury a phone call. They can't bury a whole town hearing it.

Name: e7_plan_008
Text: The transmitter powers on. But the feed line up the tower is dead. A length of coax is missing.

Name: e7_antenna_000
Text: You climb to the first platform with the cable over your shoulder. Nila talks you through it on her new radio. You fit the coax. Now the dish has to face the town.

Name: e7_antenna_001
Speaker: NILA
Text: Turn it slowly. Watch the meter. Greyhaven's somewhere south-southwest.

Name: e7_eli_000
Text: The signal meter glows green. Forty minutes to 23:00.

Name: e7_eli_001
Text: Eli arrives up the trail, out of breath, carrying a rifle from his father's closet.

Name: e7_eli_002
Speaker: ELI
Text: Tess is safe. She's with Father Tom at the church. I came to help.

Name: e7_eli_003
Text: Nila hugs him. You don't.

Name: e7_eli_004
Text: Ten minutes later you step outside to check the trip wires and hear Eli around the side of the shed, low, into a handheld radio.

Name: e7_eli_005
Speaker: ELI
Text: …Pike Point. Now. (beat) I'm sorry.

Name: e7_eli_006
Text: You round the corner. Eli turns, guilty, the radio still in his hand.

Name: e7_eli_007
Text: Across the lake, an orange glow rises over the trees: the mill is burning. On the lake road below Pike Point, a line of headlights stops at the foot of the trail.

Name: e7_eli_008
Text: The new radio on Nila's belt crackles. A man's voice, warm, amused.

Name: e7_eli_009
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Nila. Mani. And Ruth, I assume, with Harold's shotgun. (beat) Let's talk about this like adults.

Name: e7_end_000
Text: End of Episode 7.

Name: e8_open_000
Text: You grab Eli by the collar and slam him against the shed wall.

Name: e8_open_001
Speaker: MANI
Text: Who was that?

Name: e8_open_002
Speaker: ELI
Text: Ortiz! It was Ortiz! (He holds up the radio. The channel tag reads GPS-2, the deputy's private channel.) I told him to come to Pike Point with everyone he trusts.

Name: e8_open_003
Speaker: ELI
Text: I said sorry because… because I'm the reason they knew where Nila slept. I've been saying sorry to everyone all week.

Name: e8_who_000
Text: Nila looks down at the headlights on the lake road.

Name: e8_who_001
Speaker: NILA
Text: Then who brought them?

Name: e8_who_002
Speaker: JONAH
Text: Victor has a man on that water tower who sees everything. He's been watching this headland for days.

Name: e8_offer_000
Text: Victor walks up the trail alone, a flashlight in one hand, both hands visible, his coat immaculate even in the mud. Below him, four men with rifles spread into the trees. Corbin stays by the cars.

Name: e8_offer_001
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Mani! I brought no snakes, I promise.

Name: e8_offer_002
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Let's be practical. The mill's gone. Burned tonight, very sad, old wiring. There's no lab, no animals, no evidence. Just a camera, some photographs, and a very tired young woman.

Name: e8_offer_003
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Two hundred thousand dollars. Enough to bring your parents over. Enough to never write another job application.

Name: e8_offer2_000
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: No? Then something you can't buy. Corbin's video of the Marsh girl at the till goes away forever. Eli's family keeps the dock. Everyone goes home.

Name: e8_offer3_000
Text: Victor's smile thins.

Name: e8_offer3_001
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: I'm not the one you should be afraid of, Mani. My partner doesn't negotiate. If you broadcast, he'll come to Windsor himself. To your little apartment. To your parents' shop in Ranipet.

Name: e8_fail_000
Text: You hear yourself say yes. Victor smiles, warm as a fireplace. Behind you, Nila makes a sound you will hear for the rest of your life.

Name: e8_fail_001
Text: By morning the transmitter is smashed, the camera is at the bottom of the lake, and Nila won't look at you.

Name: e8_fail_002
Text: No. Not like this. Try again.

Name: e8_refuse_000
Speaker: MANI
Text: You know what my father said to me when I left India? "Look after her." That's the whole job, Victor. That's all I came here to do.

Name: e8_refuse_001
Text: Victor's smile is gone.

Name: e8_refuse_002
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Then you'll do it in the dark.

Name: e8_refuse_003
Text: He raises a hand. The floodlights on the trucks below snap on.

Name: e8_w1_000
Text: You have the revolver: six rounds. Ruth has the shotgun. Jonah has a flare gun. Eli is locked in the shed with Nila. Nila is inside warming up the transmitter for 23:00.

Name: e8_w1_001
Text: Wave one: two men moving up through the pines toward the tree line.

Name: e8_w1a_000
Text: Ruth fires twice. Bark explodes beside the first man and both of them drop flat behind a log.

Name: e8_w1a_001
Text: You fire once, carefully, when one of them raises his head. You miss. He stays down. Five rounds left.

Name: e8_w1b_000
Text: You fire three times into the dark. Two shots hit trees. The third hits a man in the leg and he goes down screaming. A rifle round sparks off the shed doorframe beside your head.

Name: e8_w1b_001
Text: Three rounds left. Your hands won't stop shaking.

Name: e8_w2_000
Text: Wave two: a man behind the shed with bolt cutters at the transmitter's power cable. At the same moment, a rifle round hits the doorframe and Jonah goes down, splinters in his arm.

Name: e8_w2a_000
Text: You round the shed. The man has the bolt cutters on the cable. You shout. He turns, and you fire. He drops the cutters and runs into the trees, holding his shoulder.

Name: e8_w2a_001
Text: Ruth is already kneeling beside Jonah, tying her scarf around his arm. He swears at her inventively. He'll live.

Name: e8_w2b_000
Text: You drag Jonah behind the doorframe. Behind the shed, a heavy clunk. The lights inside flicker. Nila shouts.

Name: e8_w2b_001
Text: You get there in time to see the man running, the cable half cut. Nila splices it with tape and swearing. It holds. Barely.

Name: e8_w3_000
Text: Wave three: a man is climbing the tower ladder to cut the antenna feed. You go up after him.

Name: e8_w3_001
Text: On the first platform, wind howling, he swings a wrench at your head.

Name: e8_w3a_000
Text: The wrench whistles over your head. You hit him low. He goes over the rail and crashes into the bushes below, groaning. Alive.

Name: e8_w3b_000
Text: The wrench catches your forearm and the revolver nearly goes over the edge. You hold on to it. You hit him with your whole body and he goes over the rail into the bushes below. Your arm screams.

Name: e8_ortiz_000
Text: No sirens come. Corbin stays by the cars, smoking, waiting. Victor's men pull back into the trees to regroup.

Name: e8_ortiz_001
Text: Ruth reloads with steady hands. "They'll come again," she says. "Do your thing, girl. Fast."

Name: e8_ortiz_002
Text: You check the revolver. One round left.

Name: e8_air_000
Text: The signal meter glows green, but only just. Jonah's spare cable is short and the needle trembles. Nila pulls on her headphones. Her hands are steady now.

Name: e8_air_001
Speaker: NILA
Text: Good evening, Greyhaven. This is After Hours on 94.1. I'm Nila. I'm back. (beat) And tonight I'm going to tell you everything.

Name: e8_air_002
Text: She looks at you. You have to hand her the proof in an order a listener, and a police officer, can follow.

Name: e8_jam_000
Text: Halfway through the ledger, the signal meter crashes to red. Nila's headphones fill with her own voice, slowed down, a few seconds behind, distorted.

Name: e8_jam_001
Speaker: JAMMING VOICE
Text: …If anyone's on seven-one-eight-five… I found it… aana andha—
Subtitle: …If anyone's on seven-one-eight-five… I found it… but don't trust the—

Name: e8_jam_002
Text: Her private voicemail to you. Only someone tapping her phone could have that.

Name: e8_jam_003
Speaker: JONAH
Text: (clutching his bleeding arm, squinting at a scope) Somebody's flooding 94.1 from the north. The water tower. Big transmitter. That's not Victor's gear.

Name: e8_jam_004
Speaker: JONAH
Text: Ruth. Your notebooks. Fourteen years of scanner channels. Find me one the provincial police listen to overnight, that he isn't covering.

Name: e8_jam_after_000
Text: The meter climbs back to green on the new channel. Nila finishes it all: the ledger, the footage, her own whisper from the bottom of the lake. She ends it the way she ended every show.

Name: e8_jam_after_001
Speaker: NILA
Text: This was After Hours. Lock your doors, Greyhaven. And thank you for listening.

Name: e8_platform_000
Text: Nila steps outside for air. A hand clamps over her mouth. Victor, mud on his coat now, a pistol in his hand, drags her up the tower ladder to the first platform.

Name: e8_platform_001
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: MANI!

Name: e8_platform_002
Text: You climb. On the platform, wind howling, Victor holds Nila at the rail with the pistol to her head. You raise the revolver. One round. Your hands shake.

Name: e8_platform_003
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: One bullet. I counted. (He laughs, breathing hard.) You're not a killer, Mani. You're a nice boy with a spreadsheet.

Name: e8_platform_004
Speaker: MANI
Text: Let her go. It's over.

Name: e8_platform_005
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Over? You think I'm the top? I'm middle management. You think he'll let me sit in a courtroom?

Name: e8_platform_006
Text: He looks north, toward the water tower, and for the first time, he looks afraid.

Name: e8_platform_007
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: He's listening right now. He's always listening. His name is—

Name: e8_platform_008
Text: A single rifle crack across the water from the north.

Name: e8_platform_009
Text: Victor jerks. He looks down at his chest, surprised. The pistol slips from his fingers.

Name: e8_platform_010
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: …Hades doesn't… leave…

Name: e8_platform_011
Text: He falls. Thirty metres into the dark pines.

Name: e8_platform_012
Text: Nila crumples into your arms. You're still holding the revolver. You never fired. On the water tower across the lake, a tiny red light blinks twice and goes dark.

Name: e8_wrong_000
Text: Headlights at the foot of the trail. Corbin's cruiser. In the back seat, a pale face against the glass. Tess.

Name: e8_wrong_001
Text: Victor's voice on the radio, very calm.

Name: e8_wrong_002
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: The Marsh girl for the little USB stick in your pocket, Mani. The encrypted one. Bring it down. Alone.

Name: e8_wrong_003
Text: You never promised to protect her. Nobody was watching her. You walk down the trail with the USB in your hand.

Name: e8_wrong_004
Text: At the bottom, Victor holds Tess by the arm. You hold out the stick. He takes it. He lets her go. She runs to you.

Name: e8_wrong_005
Speaker: VICTOR
Text: Pleasure doing business—

Name: e8_wrong_006
Text: A rifle crack from the north. Victor drops where he stands. The USB stick skitters into the dark and is gone. On the water tower, a red light blinks twice.

Name: e8_route_000
Text: The night goes very quiet.

Name: e8_dawn_000
Text: Dawn comes up grey and gold. Provincial police cruisers block the mill road. A helicopter circles the lake. The mill is a smoking shell, but the pill presses were steel and survived the fire.

Name: e8_dawn_001
Text: Corbin is arrested at the county line at six in the morning, still in uniform, a suitcase of cash on the back seat.

Name: e8_dawn_002
Text: Gus is arrested at the diner. He doesn't resist.

Name: e8_dawn_003
Text: Brian Holt is quietly escorted out of the radio station.

Name: e8_dawn_004
Text: In the trunk of Victor's car, officers find a heated travel case holding Midas and the last five golden lanceheads. A wildlife officer from Toronto says they will be sent home to Brazil.

Name: e8_dawn_005
Text: Victor's body is recovered from the pines. One rifle round, fired from more than six hundred metres, from the direction of the water tower. The tower is empty. One spent casing on the platform. Nothing else.

Name: e8_dawn_006
Text: On Victor's phone, the last incoming call: a blocked number, at 23:39. One minute before the shot.

Name: e8_bye_000
Text: For the first time, you walk through Greyhaven in daylight. Say goodbye.

Name: e8_drive_000
Text: Nila's blue hatchback, you driving, windows down despite the cold. Nila has her feet on the dashboard and the new radio in her lap. You argue about music. You laugh until your stomach hurts.

Name: e8_drive_001
Text: Your phone buzzes. An email.

Name: e8_drive_002
Text: "Thank you for your time. We'd like to invite you to a third interview next week." Nila punches your arm. "Third time's lucky. You'll get it."

Name: e8_drive_003
Text: You stop at the first Tom Portons on County Road 20. Harold and June are at the window table. Harold has a double-double. June pretends not to see.

Name: e8_drive_004
Text: Back on the road, it goes quiet. Nila watches the fields.

Name: e8_drive_005
Speaker: NILA
Text: En voicemail. "Aana andha—" Naan solla vandhadhu, badhil sollura andha kurala nambaadhannu.
Subtitle: My voicemail. "But don't trust the—" I was going to say, don't trust the voice that answers.

Name: e8_drive_006
Speaker: NILA
Text: Naan broadcast panna ovvoru raathiriyum avan badhil sonnaan. Victor avan illa, Anna. Victor-ukke avana paathu bayam.
Subtitle: Every night I broadcast, he answered. Victor wasn't him, Anna. Victor himself was scared of him.

Name: e8_drive_007
Speaker: MANI
Text: Ellam mudinjiduchu, Nila.
Subtitle: It's all over, Nila.

Name: e8_drive_008
Text: Nila doesn't answer. She turns the radio off.

Name: e8_hades_000
Text: The camera rises from the county road, back over the hill, to the old water tower above Greyhaven. On the platform stands a figure in a long dark coat, only a silhouette against the morning sun. A rifle case at his feet. A handheld radio in his gloved hand.

Name: e8_hades_001
Text: He watches a small blue car crest the hill and disappear south.

Name: e8_hades_002
Speaker: HADES
Text: Victor talked too much. It's handled. (beat) The siblings? (He watches the empty road.) No. Let them go home. Let them light their lamps.

Name: e8_hades_003
Text: He lowers the radio.

Name: e8_hades_004
Speaker: HADES
Text: I know where home is.

Name: e8_lamp_000
Text: That afternoon, alone in his cabin, Jonah plugs in a copy of the encrypted file Mani left him. "Hades_contacts.enc." He's been running it through an old decryption rig since dawn.

Name: e8_lamp_001
Text: One word in the file's header decodes. Just one. He reads it twice, then picks up his radio.

Name: e8_lamp_002
Speaker: JONAH
Text: Anna. It's Jonah. Got one word out of that file. (beat) R-E-D-L-A-K-E.

Name: e8_lamp_003
Text: He doesn't know yet what it means. Neither do you.

Name: end_daybreak_000
Text: Your small apartment in Windsor glows with clay diyas on every surface. The slightly water-damaged laddus on a steel plate. The laptop open on a video call to Vellore: Amma, Appa, oil lamps behind them, fireworks crackling in their street.

Name: end_daybreak_001
Text: Nila tells them everything herself, gently. Amma scolds you for hiding it, then thanks you, then scolds you again.

Name: end_daybreak_002
Speaker: NILA
Text: Amma, Anna-ku third interview! Adhu kooda kedaichudum.
Subtitle: Amma, Anna has a third interview! He'll get it too.

Name: end_daybreak_003
Text: Later. The call has ended. Nila is asleep on the couch under a blanket. You stand on the balcony, the Detroit skyline across the river, fireworks over both cities.

Name: end_daybreak_004
Text: Inside, on the shelf, Nila's old handheld radio, the one she carried all week, switched off. Its display flickers on by itself. One second of static. Then silence.

Name: end_daybreak_005
Text: Nobody sees it.

Name: end_daybreak_006
Text: OUT OF TOWN WILL RETURN.

Name: end_lamplight_000
Text: Diwali night. Clay diyas on every surface. Amma and Appa on the video call from Vellore, crying and laughing at once.

Name: end_lamplight_001
Text: Appa: "Nee ava-va paathukitta." (You looked after her.)

Name: end_lamplight_002
Text: Everyone you met in Greyhaven is safe. Every proof was heard. You told your parents the truth when it was hardest.

Name: end_lamplight_003
Text: Later, on the balcony, you write one word on the back of your hand so you won't forget it: REDLAKE.

Name: end_lamplight_004
Text: Inside, Nila's old radio flickers to static for one second. Nobody sees it.

Name: end_lamplight_005
Text: OUT OF TOWN WILL RETURN.

Name: e8_fog_000
Text: Somebody heard. Not enough people. Not fast enough. The signal was too weak, the proof too thin. No police come up the lake road.

Name: e8_fog_001
Text: Victor's men regroup in the trees. Corbin is shouting into his radio.

Name: e8_fog_002
Speaker: RUTH
Text: Down to the water. Now.

Name: e8_fog_003
Text: Ruth's skiff is pulled up in the reeds below the point. You, Nila, Ruth and Jonah slide down the wet slope and push off into the black water, engine off, oars only. Behind you, flashlights sweep the empty shed.

Name: e8_fog_004
Text: By sunrise you are on the highway in Nila's blue hatchback, Greyhaven a grey smudge in the mirror.

Name: e8_fog2_000
Text: Weeks later, a Toronto paper runs Nila's footage. Corbin is arrested at his kitchen table. Gus confesses. The mill is sealed.

Name: e8_fog2_001
Text: But it took weeks. And for weeks, every time it rained, Nila checked the news for Greyhaven.

Name: e8_fog2_002
Speaker: NILA
Text: Victor wasn't him, Anna. Victor was scared of him.

Name: e8_fog2_003
Text: On the water tower above Greyhaven, a silhouette in a long coat watched your car go. "I know where home is," he said, to nobody.

Name: end_fog_000
Text: Diwali in Windsor. Lamps lit, a little late. Amma and Appa on the screen. Nila thinner, quieter, alive.

Name: end_fog_001
Text: You tell yourself that's what matters. Nila is alive.

Name: end_fog_002
Text: On the shelf, her old radio clicks to static for one second. Nobody sees it.

Name: end_fog_003
Text: OUT OF TOWN WILL RETURN.

Name: e8_wrong2_000
Text: Tess shakes in your arms. Down the trail, Corbin is already in his cruiser, reversing hard. He's gone before anyone can stop him.

Name: e8_wrong2_001
Text: The broadcast went out. Police come at dawn. Corbin is caught two days later in Sault Ste. Marie.

Name: e8_wrong2_002
Text: But the encrypted file is gone, picked up from the dark by someone you never saw.

Name: e8_wrong2_003
Speaker: TESS
Text: Why didn't you watch out for me? (beat) Never mind. You came.

Name: e8_wrong2_004
Text: On the water tower, a silhouette in a long coat turns a small USB stick over in his gloved fingers. "I know where home is," he says.

Name: end_wrong_000
Text: Diwali in Windsor. Nila beside you, alive. Amma and Appa on the screen.

Name: end_wrong_001
Text: You keep thinking about the stick sliding into the dark. About what was on it. About whose hand picked it up.

Name: end_wrong_002
Text: Nila's old radio flickers to static. Nobody sees it.

Name: end_wrong_003
Text: OUT OF TOWN WILL RETURN.

Name: e8_silent_000
Text: Nobody heard. The jamming swallowed every word. No police come.

Name: e8_silent_001
Text: Ruth gets you to the water. You row in the dark with the proof in a dry bag between your knees: the camera, the ledger, the photos.

Name: e8_silent_002
Text: Three days later, in a café in Toronto, Nila hands everything to a journalist called Ivy Laurent, the one she emailed from Greyhaven months ago. Ivy goes pale reading the ledger.

Name: e8_silent_003
Speaker: IVY
Text: I know this company. I used to work for one of its suppliers. (beat) Leave it with me.

Name: e8_silent_004
Text: Greyhaven never says a word. Corbin keeps his badge for another month. Then a newspaper story runs, and he doesn't.

Name: e8_silent_005
Text: On the water tower, a silhouette in a long coat says, "I know where home is."

Name: end_silent_000
Text: Diwali in Windsor. The lamps are lit. Nila sits close to you on the couch and doesn't say much.

Name: end_silent_001
Text: The town you saved never thanked you. Maybe it never will.

Name: end_silent_002
Text: Nila's old radio flickers to static for one second. Nobody sees it.

Name: end_silent_003
Text: OUT OF TOWN WILL RETURN.
